title: "Data and student files"

## Download the classroom materials

[Download the student project ZIP](downloads/physiology-student-files.zip).
Extract it before opening files. It contains the simulated datasets, their
dictionary, a project file and the optional R example. It excludes instructor
solutions. The core practical pages supply calculation instructions that work
with a calculator and paper; opening the R project is optional.

| File | Classroom use |
| --- | --- |
| [Animal respirometry](data/animal-respirometry.csv) | Correct and interpret an oxygen-consumption measurement |
| [Plant water measurements](data/plant-water.csv) | Examine mass change and water relations |
| [Photosynthesis measurements](data/photosynthesis.csv) | Interpret a light-response series |
| [Growth and stress](data/growth-stress.csv) | Connect treatment allocation, growth and inference |
| [Data dictionary](data/README.md) | Read the design, units, column meanings and simulation provenance before calculating |

## Reuse one workflow in R, if helpful

The [optional example](optional-computing/index.qmd) repeats the animal
measurement analysis with supplied code. The project includes
[physiology.Rproj](physiology.Rproj),
[the R script](optional-computing/analysis.R) and
[the report source](optional-computing/respirometry.Rmd).
Keep the extracted directory structure intact: the report expects its data
in the supplied relative location. The optional example documents packages
and how to render from a fresh session.

## Use the data honestly

These numbers were constructed for teaching. Do not describe them as a real
experiment or use them to support a biological treatment recommendation.
Retain the raw CSV; calculate new quantities separately. Record units and
the independent experimental unit in every figure or report.
